name: অমরারাম (অমরেশ্বর মন্দির)
deity: প্রধান দেবতা হলেন অমরেশ্বর স্বামী, শিবের এক রূপ যিনি এক অস্বাভাবিক উঁচু শ্বেত লিঙ্গ রূপে প্রতিষ্ঠিত। তাঁর সঙ্গিনী এখানে বালা চামুণ্ডিকা রূপে পূজিত, মন্দিরের মাতৃদেবী।
period: ১১শ শতাব্দী খ্রিস্টাব্দ (পূর্বতর প্রাচীনত্ব ও পরবর্তী সংস্কারসহ)
dynasty: প্রাচীন সাতবাহন সংযোগ; মধ্যযুগীয় কোটা প্রধান; পরবর্তীকালে বাসিরেড্ডি বেঙ্কটাদ্রি নায়ুড়ুর পৃষ্ঠপোষকতা
summary: অমরাবতীর অমরারাম হল উপকূলীয় অন্ধ্রপ্রদেশের পাঁচটি পঞ্চারাম ক্ষেত্রের অন্যতম, যেখানে শিব এক উঁচু শ্বেত লিঙ্গের রূপে অমরেশ্বর স্বামী রূপে পূজিত। প্রাচীন বৌদ্ধ ও সাতবাহন ইতিহাসে স্তরায়িত এক শহরে কৃষ্ণা নদীর দক্ষিণ তীরে অবস্থিত, মন্দিরটি সেই তীর্থযাত্রীদের টানে যারা পাঁচটি স্থান জুড়ে সাধারণ পঞ্চারাম কিংবদন্তির অনুসরণ করেন।

sections.history: Amaravati carries a depth of history that few temple towns can match. It was a capital of the ancient Satavahana rulers and a celebrated early Buddhist centre, remembered for the great Amaravati Stupa whose carved railings are studied to this day. Tradition holds that the Amareswara lingam was installed and worshipped by Indra, lord of the devas, from whom the town takes its name as an earthly Amaravati. Over the centuries medieval patrons, among them local Kota chiefs, added to the shrine. The most far-reaching renovations are associated with Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu, the local ruler of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, whose patronage gave the temple much of its present form.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the South Indian idiom, entered through a tall gopuram and opening onto pillared halls that lead to the sanctum. Its most distinctive feature is the lingam itself, which rises to a striking height through more than one storey of the shrine. Because of this, priests perform worship at the upper portion of the lingam from a raised platform reached by an inner stair, an arrangement rarely seen elsewhere. Stone corridors, subsidiary shrines and mandapas surround the central sanctum, and the separate shrine of the goddess Bala Chamundika stands within the same complex. Later additions reflect the layered patronage the temple received, blending medieval fabric with the extensive rebuilding of more recent centuries.
sections.legends: The Pancharama Kshetras share a single origin story. According to tradition a mighty lingam once belonged to the demon Tarakasura, who could not be defeated while he wore it. In the war led by Kumara Swamy, the son of Shiva also known as Kartikeya, the lingam was broken into five pieces that fell to earth and were enshrined at five sites, of which Amararama is one. At Amaravati the lingam is further linked to Indra and the devas, who are said to have worshipped here, giving the town its name as the city of the immortals. The tall white form of Amareswara is understood as one of these five sacred fragments.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the temple's foremost festival, when devotees keep the night-long vigil and worship of Shiva. Equally important is the Kalyanotsavam, the ceremonial wedding of Amareswara Swamy and Bala Chamundika, celebrated with processions and ritual splendour. The month of Karthika, sacred to Shiva, brings large gatherings for lamp offerings and special worship on its holy days. Through these seasons the riverside town fills with pilgrims, and the temple observes its round of daily and periodic rituals with particular care.
sections.experience: A visit to Amararama joins the sacred and the historical in a single walk. The temple stands on the south bank of the Krishna, and many pilgrims pause at the river before entering. Within, the eye is drawn upward to the great lingam and to the stair by which worship reaches its upper part. The pace is unhurried and devotional rather than crowded, except on festival days. Nearby lie the remains of the ancient stupa and the museum that shelters Amaravati's Buddhist sculpture, so that a single journey can move between the living Shaiva shrine and one of India's oldest layers of built faith.

visit.timings: The temple generally opens in the early morning and again in the evening, with a midday break; exact hours and special-day timings change, so verify locally before travelling.
visit.dressCode: Modest, traditional dress is expected. Many devotees remove footwear before entering and cover the shoulders and legs as a mark of respect.
visit.photography: Photography is often restricted inside the sanctum and around the deity; look for posted notices and follow the instructions of temple staff.
visit.gettingThere: Amaravati lies near Guntur and Vijayawada in coastal Andhra Pradesh. The nearest major railway junction and airport are at Vijayawada, with the airport at Gannavaram, from where road transport reaches the temple town.
